scenes.name: quiet-week
scenes.title: A quiet week
scenes.detail: Seven days pass. The scheduled backup runs.

scenes.name: feature-release
scenes.title: Paperboat 1.1.0 is published
scenes.detail: A feature release with a schema migration.

scenes.name: cve

scenes.name: bad-release
scenes.title: Paperboat 1.2.0 is published
scenes.detail: A faulty release. The canary check must catch it.

scenes.name: kubernetes-eol
scenes.title: Kubernetes end-of-support forecast
scenes.detail: A forecast on the timeline. The local target cannot upgrade in place.

scenes.name: database-patch
scenes.title: Postgres 17.12 is pending
scenes.detail: A minor version patch of the database.

scenes.name: database-upkeep
scenes.title: Database maintenance is due
scenes.detail: Vacuum and analyze under the standing approval.

scenes.name: restore-drill
scenes.title: Monthly restore drill
scenes.detail: Restore the newest backup into a scratch database.

scenes.name: drift
scenes.title: Someone changes production by hand
scenes.detail: A manual kubectl change. The nightly drift check finds it.

scenes.name: incident
scenes.title: Incident at 02:00
scenes.detail: Inventory requests start to fail with no change in progress.

concerns: terraform.tfvars sets paperboat_version to 1.2.0-bad. The "-bad" pre-release suffix marks a build that is not a normal stable release and may be known to be faulty.

module.app.helm_release.paperboat changes values.image.tag from 1.1.1 to 1.2.0-bad. The plan only shows the tag change, so it does not show what the new image does, for example schema migrations that a rollback would not undo.

The trigger says only that 1.2.0-bad is published. That does not justify moving to a pre-release tag, so the change does not fit its stated trigger. The tag should be confirmed as intended before it is applied.

pull.title: local/50-app: upgrade Paperboat 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0
pull.body:
## What changes
`paperboat_version` in platform/stacks/local/50-app/terraform.tfvars: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0. Nothing else.

## Why now
Finding release:local:1.1.0: 1.1.0 is published and local runs 1.0.0. The release note (releases/1.1.0.md) was read.

Release summary: fish get a condition score and retire past their species' age limit. Migration 2 is a Helm pre-upgrade hook. It only adds columns, runs in one transaction and is forward-only. 1.0.0 pods keep serving during the migration and rolling update. Risk is rated Medium.

## Expected effects
- About 5 fish with the starting stock become `retired` within the first minute, as they return to their tanks. `fish_available` drops by the same number.
- `/api/inventory` gains `condition` and `retire_after_days`.

## Watch after rollout
- `fish_available` in `/api/stats`
- `aging` lines in the worker log

## Rollback
Revert this PR, which sets paperboat_version back to 1.0.0. No schema rollback is needed: 1.0.0 runs on the new schema and ignores the new columns, which stay in the database. Retirements are NOT undone by a rollback. Retired fish stay retired and need a manual data fix to restore.

work_item.trigger: Paperboat in local fails 7 of 20 inventory requests
work_item.summary: paperboat-api 1.1.1 is intermittently failing GET /api/inventory with HTTP 500 ('request handler failed'). Roughly a third of requests fail, which matches the alert's 7 of 20. The failing requests return in about 0.002 ms, so they fail before doing any real work, and successful ones take about 0.2 ms. No database, image or dependency error appears, and no change explains it. This points to bad state held in the API process's memory.

explanation.sentence: paperboat-api 1.1.1 is intermittently failing GET /api/inventory with HTTP 500 ('request handler failed'). Roughly a third of requests fail, which matches the alert's 7 of 20. The failing requests return in about 0.002 ms, so they fail before doing any real work, and successful ones take about 0.2 ms. No database, image or dependency error appears, and no change explains it. This points to bad state held in the API process's memory.
explanation.why: Alert 9: 7 of 20 inventory requests failed in local on version 1.1.1. The debug session confirms the errors continue: paperboat-api returns intermittent 500s ('request handler failed') on /api/inventory, alongside successful 200s. The pod is Running and Ready. Version 1.1.1 ran cleanly for days, the bad 1.2.0 release was already rolled back, and no recent change explains the errors. The logs show no database or dependency failure. The likely cause is corrupted in-process state in the API, which a restart should clear. I propose restart-deployment on paperboat-api. If errors persist after the restart, a human should look into the application code or its data path.
explanation.downtime: About 1 minutes of failed inventory requests
explanation.user_effect: Paperboat in local fails 7 of 20 inventory requests
pre_checks: Debug session recorded: read-only, namespace paperboat
explanation.rollback: The restart is reversible; no configuration changed
explanation.if_deferred: Mitigation: WI-0013. Evidence: The api log shows interleaved 200 and 500 responses on /api/inventory within milliseconds, with error 'request handler failed' and no other error text. The pod paperboat-api-7f4c769c76-ggvl2 is 1/1 Running and Ready with 0 restarts. The deployment is 1/1 available. Version 1.1.1 has been deployed since WI-0004, about 362h ago. The faulty 1.2.0-bad release was rolled back about 218h ago (WI-0005/WI-0006), so this is not a bad rollout. The most recent changes (Postgres minor bump, maintenance, backup, restore drill, drift check) are all Done and 2h or more old. The probe warnings in the events (connection refused at start, 503 liveness/readiness about 2m ago) are startup and transient noise. The pod is Ready now and the 500s continue.

work_item.title: Restart paperboat-api to mitigate WI-0012
work_item.summary: Runs the restart-deployment runbook under the standing approval that carol signed.

work_item.title: Run two api replicas for the holiday rush
work_item.summary: Raise the api service from one replica to two in the local environment, so it can handle more traffic during the holiday rush.

explanation.sentence: Raise the api service from one replica to two in the local environment, so it can handle more traffic during the holiday rush.
explanation.why: Carol Reyes opened a pull request to run two api replicas for the holiday rush (WI-0014). The plan changes one setting: the api replica count goes from 1 to 2.
explanation.downtime: The plan does not state any planned outage. It updates the existing paperboat Helm release in place and creates or destroys nothing.
explanation.user_effect: Users should see the same app. Requests can now be spread across two api instances, which should help when traffic is high.
explanation.cost_change: The plan does not state a cost figure. The second api replica will use additional compute while it runs.
explanation.duration: The plan does not state how long the update takes.
pre_checks: The plan is current. It is not superseded.
The plan matches the reviewed change, and the pipeline enforces this.
The only resource change is updating module.app.helm_release.paperboat.
No resources are added, replaced, or destroyed.
explanation.backup: No backup is needed for this change. The plan changes no stateful resources and no identities.
explanation.rollback: Set the api replica count back to 1 and apply the plan again. The plan outputs a release_revision, so the previous Helm revision is also available as a fallback.
explanation.verification: Confirm the apply finishes and reports the new release_revision. Then confirm the api runs two replicas and that the paperboat release is healthy.
explanation.if_deferred: The api keeps running with one replica. If traffic rises during the holiday rush, there is less capacity to absorb it. The plan was created on 2026-12-16, so if the code changes before approval, a new plan will be needed.
